replies.body: `getPom(jarFile, jarEntry)` runs before `getManifest(jarFile, jarEntry)` in `forUrl`, and both start by opening the same `new JarInputStream(jarFile.getInputStream(jarEntry))` — whose constructor is what parses the manifest. Any `IOException` from a missing/corrupt embedded jar or unreadable manifest is thrown by `getPom` first, so `getManifest` is never reached. Swallowing here vs. propagating produces the same outcome in practice; leaving it as-is.

This won't work for paths with spaces since in url space is encoded with `%20`. For ideas see https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/blob/3184eb3acc8e2e6e95623c43e979ef6c256887ed/spring-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/util/ResourceUtils.java#L324
This can be annoyingly complicated since the urls can be malformed. For example as far as I remember websphere by default doesn't encode spaces to `%20`.
